findings.summary: `gc` is used as a recovery limit before it is introduced or explained.
findings.evidence: Reflog ~90 days; unreachable ~30 days, until gc
findings.fix: Add a short gloss on page 1, for example 'gc = git's garbage collection, which permanently deletes unreferenced commits'.

findings.summary: The 'What Can Be Lost' table lumps two different expiry windows into one cell, which is confusing.
findings.evidence: Committed | Reflog ~90 days; unreachable ~30 days, until gc
findings.fix: Split into two rows (reachable ~90 days, unreachable ~30 days) or point to the Time Limit section on page 5.

findings.summary: The 'Three Areas' list is plain text where a diagram would show the flow between areas.
findings.evidence: Working tree / files on disk / Index / staging, git add / Repository / HEAD commit, git commit
findings.fix: Add a diagram: Working tree -> (git add) -> Index -> (git commit) -> Repository.

findings.summary: The older-equivalents table pairs `git checkout <c> -- <file>` with `git restore --source=<c> <file>`, but the two commands are not equivalent.
findings.fix: `git checkout <c> -- <file>` updates both the index and the worktree. Its modern equivalent is `git restore --source=<c> --staged --worktree <file>`. Change the table row, or add a note that the plain restore form touches only the worktree.

findings.summary: The older-equivalents table maps `git checkout <c> -- <file>` to `git restore --source=<c> <file>`, but the two do different things.
findings.fix: Map it to `git restore --source=<c> --staged --worktree <file>`, because the checkout form updates both the index and the working tree. Or note that plain `--source` touches only the working tree.

findings.summary: `HEAD~2` is used on page 2 and `HEAD~1`/`HEAD~3` on page 3, but the `~N` notation is never explained.
findings.evidence: --source takes any commit: HEAD~2, a branch, a tag
findings.fix: Add one line: 'HEAD~N means N commits before the current tip'.

findings.summary: The code block for restore appears before the one-line idea behind each command, and the caption crams three results into one line.
findings.evidence: git restore --source=HEAD~2 app.py ... old content into worktree; into both; chosen hunks only
findings.fix: Annotate each command inline with its own comment instead of one combined caption.

findings.summary: The '-p' bullet holds multiple ideas and mixes two concepts: the prompt options and the effect on other hunks.
findings.evidence: -p asks per hunk: y discard, n keep, s split
findings.fix: Split into: '-p asks per hunk' and 'y discard, n keep, s split the hunk'.

findings.summary: The reset page explains the modes in a table but never shows the three areas moving; the 'Moves' column is hard to map to the areas defined on page 1.
findings.evidence: --soft | HEAD | staged; --mixed (default) | HEAD + index | unstaged, still on disk
findings.fix: Use the area names from page 1 (Repository, Index, Working tree) in the table columns and add a diagram of what each mode rewinds.

findings.summary: The ORIG_HEAD bullet holds two ideas and the term 'tip' is used without definition.
findings.evidence: ORIG_HEAD records the previous tip, so it undoes a bad merge or reset
findings.fix: Split into 'ORIG_HEAD records where HEAD was before a risky move' and 'reset --hard ORIG_HEAD undoes a bad merge or reset'.

findings.summary: The amend and revert bullets pack several ideas each, and the revert code block comes before a one-line summary of each variant.
findings.evidence: Fix its message, or stage more files and add them without a new commit
findings.fix: Split into one bullet per use case and annotate each command line with its own comment.

findings.summary: The recovery table mixes a recipe for a dropped stash with a reflog-based lookup, and the 'git branch -D' note sits inside the table region as a loose fragment.
findings.evidence: Dropped stash / dangling commit | git fsck --lost-found | git branch <name> <hash>
findings.fix: Move the 'git branch -D deletes the label only' fact out of the table into its own bullet under the deleted-branch recipe.

findings.summary: The expiry window is stated here as 'Reachable entries expire after 90 days', but page 1 says 'Committed ... Reflog ~90 days' with different wording, so the terms 'reachable' and 'committed' are used inconsistently.
findings.evidence: Reachable entries expire after 90 days / Unreachable entries expire after 30 days vs. 'Committed | Reflog ~90 days; unreachable ~30 days'
findings.fix: Use the same terms ('reachable' and 'unreachable') on both pages.
